title: Developer Pathways: Maturity Mapping & Initiative Tracker
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a coherent, measurable developer 'pathways' program that maps SDKs, docs, and quickstarts into a maturity model (Discover → Try → Integrate → Scale) and provides an operational tracker for initiatives, signals, and remediation. The tracker will become the single source of truth for PM/Eng/Design on experiments, rollout status, and OKR progress for DX programs.

Why now: Activation metrics are flat for new signups despite increasing traffic. Teams report fragmented signals (separate SDK metrics, docs visits, and sample-app usage) and ambiguous handoffs from sample -> production. We need a productized approach that ties concrete outcomes to each stage of the developer journey and makes trade-offs explicit (time→activation, effort→retention, time→cost).

Scope: 1) Maturity model definition and mapping for all official SDKs, sample apps, core quickstarts and docs flows. 2) A roadmap of initiatives (experiments, content rewrites, SDK ergonomics) mapped to pathway stages, owners, and cycle-level milestones. 3) A lightweight tracker (sheet + dashboard) surfaced to the DX guild and Leadership that maps initiatives to OKRs, signals (activation, time-to-first-success, sample-pr-to-prod conversion), and risks.

Out of scope (initial): Full automation of signal ingestion (we will instrument and manually upload signals in Cycle 1) and deep personalization of pathways per customer segment (future work).
maturity_model: Discover: discoverability + initial curiosity (docs search, marketing quickstarts, sample-app landing)
Try: frictionless first success (npm/pypi install, minimal call to RDW API, first token throughput positive)
Integrate: developer integrates SDK into their app, tests locally, CI/CD proof points
Scale: long-term usage, cost/perf guardrails, onboarding to Dedicated/Private if needed
okrs_linked: OKR-DX-2026-Q2: Increase developer activation rate (TFFS) by 30%
OKR-COMM-2026-Q2: Reduce time-to-first-success for sample apps by 40%
OKR-COST-2026-Q2: Reduce per-token test cost for trial cohorts by 20%
signals_and_metrics: time_to_first_success (TFFS): median seconds from signup->successful API call
sample_app_pr_to_prod_conversion: percent of sample-app users that reach a second commit in 14 days
sdk_install_success_rate: percentage of installs that complete without errors (first-attempt)
docs_task_completion_rate: % of docs users who follow a quickstart end-to-end
trial_retention_7d: retention of trial accounts that completed a quickstart
milestones: M1: Maturity model and mapping complete (2026-03-01)
M2: Baseline signals collected and uploaded to tracker (2026-03-20)
M3: 3 prioritized initiatives scoped and resourced (2026-04-05)
prioritized_initiatives: Init-A SDK ergonomic: reduce friction for Python SDK install and auth (owner: ENG-5123)
Init-B Docs quickstarts: convert 2 legacy quickstarts to 'minimal-first-success' flow with reproducible artifacts (owner: DES-1041)
Init-C Sample-app gating: add CI/CD smoke tests and cost-estimation badges to sample apps (owner: ENG-4210)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signals are inconsistent between telemetry sources → Mitigation: canonical ingestion sheet + manual vetting before automating.
Risk: Engineering bandwidth limited in Q2 → Mitigation: reduce scope of experiments to A/B toggles and docs-only variants for Cycle 1.
Risk: Changes increase trial costs → Mitigation: add cost guardrails and sample traffic caps; run on small cohorts first.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A public maturity map (confluence link) that lists stage, mapped artifacts, and owner for each SDK/docs/quickstart.
AC2: Tracker contains baseline signals for every mapped artifact and is refreshed weekly for Cycle 1.
AC3: At least 2 Cycle-1 experiments with clear measurement plans and owners launched by M4.
AC4: Executive one-pager summarizing progress vs OKRs available by M5.
communication_plan: Weekly sync with DX guild (Wednesdays, 30m) -> share tracker updates and blockers
Bi-weekly stakeholder readout (PM/Eng/Design leads) with heatmap of initiative status
Confluence: single 'Developer Pathways' page with living maturity map and links to artifacts
Slack channel #dx-pathways for day-to-day updates, tagging owners for action items
